note: Herald Square shoppers, tourists, holiday strollers.

lines.text: Hello! Isn't it wonderful? I've never seen so many people.
Excuse me, is this the line for the store?
There's a sale on the fourth floor. Everyone's running.
I came for a toaster. I'm leaving with a toaster and a lamp.
Which way is the Empire Estate Building? Oh. Up. Of course.
Hold your purse. My cousin says hold your purse.
First time in New York. My feet are already sorry.
Prices! Everything's gone up. Even the pretzels.
Escalator's packed. I'll take the stairs. Nine floors.
Rain! And these are suede!
Duck inside the store! It's air-conditioned!
It's hotter here than Florida. And Florida's hot.
Goodness! These drivers!
We're crossing! We have the light!
Oh! Pardon me. My bags!
Excuse you! Some manners!
Was that a thief? Did he take something?
He's running for the sale! Let's go!
Help! That car's on the sidewalk!
The store went dark! Where's the exit?
Lights out. Well, no more shopping. Thank God.
Square's empty after nine. Kind of spooky.
Look at the parade of windows. Like a movie.
I saw a man on a ladder hanging a sign as big as a house!
Could you take our picture? No, the camera's simple. Just push.
My husband's at the hardware counter. Since noon.
Shopping in a city that's going broke. Somebody has to.
Hot pretzel? Best thing on Thirty-Fourth Street.
Is it always this wet? It looked dry in the brochure.
Sorry, dear. Crowded. Everyone's crowded.
Are those the World Trading Towers down there? So tall!
